### Executive Summary
- **PaperCut NG/MF vulnerabilities are now in CISA KEV with reports of active intrusions/data theft**—treat any exposed PaperCut as potentially compromised until proven otherwise.
- **Multiple “edge/perimeter” and high-impact PoCs surfaced (FortiOS auth bypass, PAN-OS GlobalProtect RCE, NetScaler auth bypass)**—prioritize exposure validation and threat hunting on remote-access infrastructure.
- **Credential/session theft and LPE tooling noise is rising (infostealers targeting SaaS/AI sessions; new Windows LPE PoC + unverified Kaspersky EPP LPE claim)**—tighten token/session monitoring and watch for post-exploitation escalation.

---

### High-priority items (immediate attention)

**1) PaperCut NG/MF — KEV + active exploitation/intrusions**
- **What happened:** CISA added **PaperCut NG/MF** flaws (reported as CVE-2026-81578 and CVE-2026-82078) to **KEV**; multiple sources report exploitation escalating to intrusions/data theft.
- **Why it matters operationally:** PaperCut often runs on Windows servers with broad AD reach; exploitation commonly becomes a fast path to **domain foothold + lateral movement** in enterprise networks.
- **Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today:** Validate if **any PaperCut is internet-reachable**; prioritize patch/mitigation + isolate if uncertain; start compromise checks (new admin accounts/services, suspicious child processes from PaperCut services, unusual outbound from PaperCut host).

**2) Perimeter access stack risk — FortiOS auth bypass PoC + PAN-OS GlobalProtect RCE PoC + NetScaler auth bypass analysis**
- **What happened:** Public PoCs/analysis circulated for **FortiOS auth bypass (CVE-2024-55591)**, **PAN-OS GlobalProtect command injection/RCE (CVE-2024-3400)**, and **NetScaler ADC/Gateway auth bypass (CVE-2026-19490)**.
- **Why it matters operationally:** These are commonly internet-facing appliances; successful exploitation can lead to **credential theft, config tampering, VPN session abuse, and rapid ransomware staging**.
- **Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today:** Confirm inventory/exposure (CMDB + external scan + WAF/VPN VIPs); review last 7–14 days for **anomalous admin logins/config changes**; ensure latest vendor mitigations/patches are applied and restrict management interfaces to trusted IPs.

**3) Identity/Auth bypass themes — Keycloak (Red Hat) auth bypass + Pangolin auth bypass**
- **What happened:** New disclosures include **Keycloak on Red Hat auth bypass (CVE-2026-9798)** and **Pangolin pre-1.22.0 auth bypass (CVE-2026-72001)** (no public exploit noted for Keycloak).
- **Why it matters operationally:** Auth bypass on IdP/proxy layers can enable **unauthorized access to protected apps** and stealthy session establishment without password guessing.
- **Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today:** Identify any **Keycloak** deployments and verify version/advisory status; add temporary detections for **unexpected auth success paths** (logins without normal factors/flows) and unusual spikes in token issuance/redirect patterns.

**4) Credential/session theft uptick — infostealers targeting SaaS sessions (incl. Anthropic/Claude)**
- **What happened:** Reporting indicates threat actors using **infostealers to steal session material** (cookies/tokens) to access accounts; broader infostealer activity noted hitting major vendors/users.
- **Why it matters operationally:** SOC and engineering users may reuse browsers/profiles across work SaaS; stolen sessions can bypass MFA and enable **data access + persistence via API keys**.
- **Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today:** Hunt for **impossible travel / abnormal user-agent / new device** signals in SSO/SaaS; force re-authentication and revoke sessions for suspicious accounts; remind staff not to install “helper” tools/extensions and keep EDR tamper protections enforced.

---

### Monitoring & detection recommendations
- **PaperCut servers (Windows/Linux):** EDR + Windows Security logs (4688/4697/7045) for PaperCut service spawning shells/utilities; hunt for webshell-like activity and unusual outbound (MITRE **T1190**, **T1059**, **T1105**).
- **VPN/edge appliances (Fortinet/Palo Alto/NetScaler):** VPN/firewall/admin audit logs for **new admin users**, config export, policy changes, and login anomalies; alert on management access from new geos/IPs (MITRE **T1078**, **T1562**).
- **Web exploitation patterns:** WAF/reverse-proxy logs for spikes in 4xx/5xx, traversal/command-injection strings, and repeated requests to auth endpoints; correlate with backend process creation on the same host (MITRE **T1190**).
- **Identity (Keycloak/SSO):** IdP logs for **unexpected auth success**, token issuance volume spikes, abnormal redirect URIs, and sessions created without typical MFA step-up (MITRE **T1556**, **T1606**).
- **Infostealers/session theft:** EDR detections for credential access from browsers (Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile reads), suspicious archive/exfil tools, and unusual processes accessing cookie stores (MITRE **T1555**, **T1005**, **T1041**).
- **Privilege escalation on endpoints:** Watch for exploitation chaining after initial access—new LPE PoCs (e.g., Windows kernel streaming LPE) increase risk of **rapid SYSTEM escalation**; alert on token manipulation and high-integrity process spawning from user context (MITRE **T1068**, **T1134**).
- **Email-to-code execution (legacy but resurfacing):** Given renewed PoC chatter (e.g., Follina), keep email gateway + EDR tuned for Office spawning msdt/powershell/cmd; quarantine suspicious attachments/links (MITRE **T1204**, **T1059**).

---

### Medium-term follow-ups
- **Patch governance:** Re-validate patch SLAs for **internet-facing** systems (print mgmt, VPNs, gateways, IdP); ensure KEV items trigger emergency change windows.
- **Exposure management:** Add continuous external discovery for “shadow IT” services (e.g., PaperCut instances, admin portals) and enforce **management plane allowlisting**.
- **Session hygiene program:** Standardize rapid response for session theft—session revocation playbooks, conditional access “new device” step-up, and API key rotation procedures.
- **Hardening:** Ensure EDR tamper protection on all endpoints; restrict local admin rights; enforce application allowlisting for high-risk user groups (SOC/IT admins).
- **Vendor follow-up (uncertain claims):** Track the **unverified Kaspersky Endpoint LPE** claim—assume possible until vendor confirms; ensure product is updated and monitor vendor advisories before taking disruptive action.
